concepts.title: One miss, no rescue.
concepts.rationale: The card turns parlay math into one visible equation: two required outcomes mean one miss ends the ticket, which is the key cost mechanism many players miss when they compare payouts first.
concepts.caption: A two-leg parlay can look attractive, but both independent 50% results must still happen together. The board uses 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4, so about 1 in 4 tickets lands at that illustrative level. Build your session around entertainment, not a guaranteed combo.
concepts.alt: Playbook sports card on navy background titled One miss, no rescue. A parlay board shows Leg 1 and Leg 2 as independent 50% outcomes, then a formula to 1/4 and a 25% (about 1 in 4) result row. A takeaway says one in four two-leg parlays at this illustrative level. A protected footer shows helpline and age disclaimer placeholders.

sources.note: The table in Parlays lists 2-leg parlay approximate payout around 2.6:1 and approximate probability around 1 in 4; this supports showing multiplication of two leg outcomes into a one-in-four result.
The section emphasizes pricing effects on parlays and the compounded margin. This supports the card’s reminder to check the legs before considering payout language.

concepts.title: Hot streaks are loud, not lucky.
concepts.rationale: A short myth/fact callout contrasts the emotional feel of a streak with the actual independence of slots outcomes, with the key 0% change figure held visually in one line.
concepts.caption: Three wins in a row are memorable, but they do not improve the next spin. Slots are random every pull, and the machine does not remember your last result. One result does not predict the next.
concepts.alt: Playbook myth card on navy background titled Hot streaks are loud, not lucky. A myth/fact label indicates 0% of prior results affecting the next spin. A two-column panel shows Last result, Next spin change at 0%, and Next spin odds listed as same as before, with a takeaway that each spin is independent. A footer with protected placeholders closes the card.

sources.note: The section states every slot spin is statistically independent and machines do not keep score. The card’s 0% change line directly reflects this claim and the myth line in the article explainer.
The tip section ends with the same principle: each spin is independent and previous outcomes do not affect the next result.

concepts.title: Same edge. Bigger bill.
concepts.rationale: The concept uses a simple 5% edge table to show why bankroll control matters: changing the stake changes money at risk proportionally while the edge percentage stays constant.
concepts.caption: A 5% house edge means expected loss is a percentage of total stake. A game with 95% RTP has about a 5% house edge long-run. On $1, expected loss is about $0.05; on $10, $0.50. Let long-run percentages guide your budget, not a one-spin result.
concepts.alt: Playbook budget-control card on navy background titled Same edge. Bigger bill. A 5% house edge board displays four rows comparing $1, $10, $100, and $1,000 stakes/wagers. The values show expected long-run losses of $0.05, $0.50, $5, and $50, reinforcing that the house-edge percentage stays fixed while dollar amounts scale. The action line says House edge fixed. Dollar amounts scale. Protected helpline and age placeholders appear in the footer.

sources.note: The section defines house edge as the percentage of total wagers kept by the game and gives typical RTP ranges. 95% RTP corresponds to 5% house edge, which is used for the expected-loss examples.

sources.section: Myth 6: Higher Bets Improve Your Odds
sources.note: The myth entry explicitly states house-edge percentage is fixed across stake sizes and larger bets scale both wins and losses. The table applies that rule to an illustrative 95% RTP (5% edge) example.

notes: Sports concept shows a two-leg two independent 50% assumption explicitly; 1 in 4 is an outcome-level illustration and does not claim a guaranteed short-term hit rate. Myth concept uses independent-spin wording from cited references. Wildcard values are long-run expected-loss illustrations using 95% RTP / 5% house-edge and do not guarantee any single-spin result.
